k1p1-2.name: text#2
k1p1-2.text: KP01 A neuron adds signals, fires past a threshold

k1p1-28.name: text#28
k1p1-28.text: accumulate $\to$ pass the threshold $\to$ fire: the mechanism, not the shape

k1p2-2.name: text#2
k1p2-2.text: It is a switch, not a volume knob

k1p2-25.name: text#25
k1p2-25.text: $z=2$ and $z=3$ both give 1: the output only asks whether the bar was crossed

k1p3-2.name: text#2
k1p3-2.text: Write the mechanism as one formula

k1p4-2.name: text#2
k1p4-2.text: By hand: same inputs, different thresholds

k1p4-38.name: text#38
k1p4-38.text: $\theta=2$: $s=0$ just reaches the bar, so it still fires

k1p4-40.name: text#40
k1p4-40.text: the total never changes, only the threshold: outputs 1, 1, 0

k1p5-22.name: text#22
k1p5-22.text: $s\ge0$ versus $s>0$ is only a convention; keep one in a whole computation

k1p5-24.name: text#24
k1p5-24.text: the step: 0 on the left, 1 from $s=0$ onward

k1p6-2.name: text#2
k1p6-2.text: Only the bias changes: AND or OR

k1p6-26.name: text#26
k1p6-26.text: solid: output 1 · open: output 0 · dashed: the decision line $s=0$

k1p6-28.name: text#28
k1p6-28.text: one neuron: $w_0=-2$ is AND, $w_0=-1$ is OR

k1p7-2.name: text#2
k1p7-2.text: A NOT gate needs a negative weight

k1p7-17.name: text#17
k1p7-17.text: When the input goes 0 $\to$ 1 the output must go 1 $\to$ 0

k1p7-18.name: text#18
k1p7-18.text: so $s$ must shrink: the weight must be negative. With all weights positive, a bigger input can only grow $s$, so NOT is impossible.

k1p8-2.name: text#2
k1p8-2.text: What this neuron lacks is learning

k1p8-7.name: text#7
k1p8-7.text: add the signals, fire only past a threshold

k1p8-9.name: text#9
k1p8-9.text: change only the threshold or weights: AND, OR, NOT

k1p8-11.name: text#11
k1p8-11.text: McCulloch and Pitts: a network of them computes any logic function

k1p8-13.name: text#13
k1p8-13.text: A person must work out the weights and threshold beforehand. Can we give only data and right answers and let it fix its own weights?

k1p8-30.name: text#30
k1p8-30.text: next unit: the Perceptron learns its own weights

steps.label: KP01 A neuron adds signals, fires past a threshold
A biological neuron · 1/8
steps.speakerNotes: An artificial neuron copies the mechanism of a biological one. First, four parts.

steps.label: A biological neuron · 1/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Dendrites act like antennas; each receives one signal.

steps.label: A biological neuron · 1/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The soma adds the received signals together, with the nucleus inside.

steps.label: A biological neuron · 1/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Only when the total crosses a threshold does it fire along the axon and, through the synapse, to the next neuron; otherwise it stays silent.

steps.label: Switch, not knob · 2/8
steps.speakerNotes: One threshold, three totals. The bar length is the total z.

steps.label: Switch, not knob · 2/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Total 1 misses the bar and stays silent; total 2 just reaches it and fires; total 3 exceeds it and also fires.

steps.label: Switch, not knob · 2/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: z = 2 and z = 3 give the same output. The output only says whether the threshold was crossed; stronger input does not give a bigger output.

steps.label: Switch, not knob · 2/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: So it is a switch.

steps.label: Weighted sum, bias, activation · 3/8
steps.speakerNotes: Map each biological piece to a mathematical one. Signals become inputs and the importance of each becomes a weight.

steps.label: Weighted sum, bias, activation · 3/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Signals become inputs x; the importance of each becomes a weight w.

steps.label: Weighted sum, bias, activation · 3/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The threshold moves into the bias, w0 equals minus theta; fire or stay silent becomes the activation f.

steps.label: Weighted sum, bias, activation · 3/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Together this is the 1943 McCulloch–Pitts neuron: weighted sum plus bias, then a step. Sum at least theta and s at least 0 are the same condition.

steps.label: Three thresholds by hand · 4/8
steps.speakerNotes: Main example: three inputs 1, 0, 1 with all weights 1. The total z is 2; the input 0 contributes nothing.

steps.label: Three thresholds by hand · 4/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Threshold 1: s is 1, output 1. Threshold 2: s is 0, output 1. Threshold 3: s is minus 1, output 0.

steps.label: Three thresholds by hand · 4/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: At threshold 2, s is 0 and just reaches the bar, so the neuron still fires; this is why the step uses at least 0.

steps.label: Three thresholds by hand · 4/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The total never changed; only the threshold did.

steps.label: The step function · 5/8
steps.speakerNotes: The activation is a step: output 0 when s is below 0, output 1 when s is at least 0. The solid dot sits above s equals 0, the open dot below.

steps.label: The step function · 5/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Put the three s values from the last page on it: s equal 1 and 0 are on the firing level, s equal minus 1 on the silent level.

steps.label: The step function · 5/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: At least versus greater than is only a convention; use one throughout. This unit uses at least.

steps.label: The step function · 5/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Zero on the left, one from zero on.

steps.label: AND and OR · 6/8
steps.speakerNotes: Two inputs, all weights 1, bias minus 2: s reaches 0 only when both inputs are 1; that is AND. The four corners have s equal minus 2, minus 1, minus 1, 0.

steps.label: AND and OR · 6/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Bias minus 1: s reaches 0 as soon as one input is 1; that is OR. The four corners have s equal minus 1, 0, 0, 1.

steps.label: AND and OR · 6/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The dashed line is the decision line s equals 0. The same neuron, differing only in bias, is a different gate.

steps.label: AND and OR · 6/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: But a person worked out the weights and bias beforehand.

steps.label: The NOT gate · 7/8
steps.speakerNotes: NOT has one input. Take weight minus 1 and bias 0.5.

steps.label: The NOT gate · 7/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Input 0: s is 0.5, output 1.

steps.label: The NOT gate · 7/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Input 1: s is minus 0.5, output 0. A bigger input lowers s, so the weight must be negative; a neuron with all-positive weights cannot make NOT.

steps.label: The NOT gate · 7/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The sign of a weight decides whether that input promotes or inhibits.

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8
steps.speakerNotes: The whole unit is about this one formula.

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Three points: add signals and fire only past a threshold; changing only the threshold or weights gives AND, OR, NOT; McCulloch and Pitts showed networks of them compute any logic function.

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: But a person must work out the weights. Can we give only data and right answers and let it correct itself? The next unit's Perceptron is the answer.

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The neuron already has computing power; what it lacks is learning.
